extending the shared `_write_fake_cli` so `plan validate` fails whenever `--repo-root` equals the plugin root conflates the #4490 defect path with the legitimate `_consumer_repo_root() or plugin_root` fallback. after the production fix, many existing `test_design_publish.py` success-path cases still run without a consumer git cwd (tmp_path fixtures, no `git init`, no `cwd=str(consumer)`), so `_consumer_repo_root()` returns `none` and validation correctly falls back to `plugin_root`. a global fake-validator failure on plugin `--repo-root` would flip those tests to `validate_status=defects-found` / `publish_rc=4` even though the production fix is correct.

a regression test that proves the fix only via fake-validator failure on plugin `--repo-root` plus publish success does not pin the contract the bug violated: composed-plan validation must receive consumer `--repo-root` while `claude_plugin_root` stays on the plugin cache. a publish-success-only check can pass if the fake always returns ok.

the proposed `_write_recording_cli` in `python/test_design_publish.py` mirrors the postplan recording harness, which only special-cases `plan validate` and otherwise exits 0 with empty stdout. full `design publish` runs a longer subprocess tail after validate (`redact secrets`, `named-block write`, `tracking-issue rename`, `design log-publish`, and optionally `diagrams upsert`). after validate records the correct `repo_root` / `claude_plugin_root`, `publish_core` hits `redact secrets`, receives exit 0 with empty stdout from the fake fallback, and returns rc 5 (`design_publish.py` ~294-295) before `plan_write_ok=true` or planned `validate_status=ok` / no-`publish_rc=4` assertions run. the regression test therefore cannot pass as written and does not reliably exercise the validate root contract.
